title: The planner uses an index only when it makes the query read less
caption: Random index lookups cost more per row than a sequential read, so for a large share of the table the seq scan wins.

steps.text: 1. Is there an index whose leading column(s) match the filter? WHERE lower(email) = … can't use a plain index on email.
2. No index: read every heap page. Fine for a 10k-row table, a disaster on the hot path of a 100M-row one.
3. Index exists: estimate selectivity from table statistics. Will the filter match a small fraction of rows?
4. Yes (one user, one order, the last hour): descend the B-tree and fetch just those pages.
5. No (status = 'active' on 80% of rows): one sequential pass beats millions of random page reads, so the planner ignores the index. Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE to see the choice.
